messages.subject: Working of Rhipe
parts:
Hi,
i would like to know that how exactly the Rhipe works.
Well i understand that

(1 ) Rhipe uses the Hadoop streaming facility to run the map reduce
jobs. It encapsulates the map and reduce expression along with the
other Hadoop related parameters and then it uses the Hadoop Streaming
facility to submit the jobs.

(2) The map and reduce programs runs on the R environment.

Now the mapper and reducer tasks has to run on the JVM,
Q1) So how JVM runs the map and reduce function on the R environment?

Q2) What is happening internally? How does the sorting and shuffling
is taking place?

A more general question is that why the Rhipe needs to installed on
all the nodes? Since anyways the Rhipe submits the job to the Hadoop
and its the hadoop MapReduce framework that parallelize the
application, so is it not sufficient to install the Rhipe only on the
namenode of the hadoop as the PIG does?

Regards,
Sharma

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Working of Rhipe
parts:
>
> (1 ) Rhipe uses the Hadoop streaming facility to run the map reduce
> jobs. It encapsulates the map and reduce expression along with the
> other Hadoop related parameters and then it uses the Hadoop Streaming
> facility to submit the jobs.
>
> (2) The map and reduce programs runs on the R environment.
>
> Now the mapper and reducer  tasks has to run on the JVM,
> Q1) So how JVM runs the map and reduce function on the R environment?

Starts R in the subprocess and feeds data via standard input and
reads from standard output and standard error
Other options a) use a local tcp/ip port but i think on linux, writing
and reading from standard * is very fast
or b) embed R using JNI - not sure if there any benefit here. There is
a rough cut on Github which doesn't
give correct results for combiners. Not sure if there is any
performance improvement (and whether it's worth all the JNI hassle)

>
> Q2) What  is happening internally? How does the sorting and shuffling
> is taking place?

Hadoop does sorting and shuffling. Default ordering is byte ordering
but you can sort on numeric values and string values
(even with vectors so that shorter vectors come before longer ones)
and partition on slices of the vector (if it is a
string/numeric/integer vector)

>
> A more general question is that why the Rhipe needs to installed on
> all the nodes? Since anyways the Rhipe submits the job to the Hadoop
> and its the hadoop MapReduce framework that parallelize the
> application, so is it not sufficient to install the Rhipe only on the
> namenode of the hadoop as the PIG does?
>

It can be done...see rhoptions()$runner, so one approach would be to

x <- rhoptions()$runner[1]
rhput(x,"/tmp/") # copy tp the DFS
rhoptions()$runner[1] = "./imperious.so"
rhmr(...., shared.files= c("/tmp/imperious.so")....)

It is crucial all the directories and paths are identical across
nodes. This /might/ work - try it out.
Don't have a cluster at hand right now to confirm.

Cheers
Saptarshi
